title: Cipher telegrams to Setembrino de Carvalho, federal commander in Ceará (Juazeiro sedition)
correspondents: Rio de Janeiro (Pamplona and others) → Fernando Setembrino de Carvalho
shelfmark: CPDOC/FGV, Arquivo Fernando Setembrino de Carvalho, FSC pce 1914.03.10/4
folio_note: 16 images (DocReader bib FSC_PACEARA pagfis 1317-1332): 12 telegrams 10 Mar - 20 May 1914, 10 with cipher (~200 words, most repeated as service check), from Pamplona, Vespasiano de Albuquerque and Rego Barros. Pencil decipherment of the whole cipher text on the 14 Mar telegram (pagfis 1319); pencil attempt on two words of pagfis 1326. Transcription sample: research/latam_vetting/1470_sample.txt.
status: CPDOC summary 'Telegramas cifrados a Setembrino de Carvalho'. Image of the first telegram viewed 28 Oct 2026: letter cipher, no decipherment on the sheet. Cribs in the same digitised fonds: FSC cont 1914.10.07/2 (two War Ministry cipher words glossed) and FSC pce 1914.02.19/2 (typed clear copies of Vespasiano's telegrams to Setembrino, one acknowledging 'mais dois cifrados'). Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Vetted 28 Oct 2026: Vigenère, 8-letter key restarted per word; key MFTDBSJV rebuilt from the pencil decipherment on pagfis 1319 reads the Mar-Apr telegrams; 10 Mar (LETCARIV, garbled) and 20 May (about 10-letter key) broke ciphertext-only in minutes. Verdict key_lookup: a small, quick reading, worth doing as a target (key recovered from adjacent plaintext / ciphertext-only), not a catalogue entry.
why: Government cipher traffic during the 1914 federal intervention against the Juazeiro (Padre Cícero) rising in Ceará; Brazilian army/government cipher of 1914 otherwise unknown.
score_note: Scored from the CPDOC description and one image during the Oct 2026 Brazil sweep (research/latam_brazil/)
verify: Page through the 16 images in DocReader; transcribe the groups; test periodic polyalphabetic (Vigenère/Beaufort, Portuguese) and code hypotheses; look for decipherments in neighbouring FSC pce 1914 folders.
prior_art: no prior reading found except the contemporary pencil decipherment of the 14 Mar telegram (checked 28 Oct 2026: DECODE dumps, known.py, web search)

seen.where: https://www.docvirt.com/docreader.net/docreader.aspx?bib=FSC_PACEARA&pasta=FSC%20pce%201914.03.10/4 (pagfis 1317-1332, all 16 images viewed and downloaded at 1663 px wide on 28 Oct 2026); related telegram FSC cont 1914.10.07/2 at bib FSC_CONTEST pagfis 587.
seen.extent: 16 images, 12 telegrams of 10 Mar - 20 May 1914 to Setembrino de Carvalho: 10 with cipher (about 200 cipher words in all, most sent twice, body and service repeat), one clear (pagfis 1318) and one clear signature sheet (1323). Senders: E. Pamplona (1317, 1327), the Minister of War Vespasiano de Albuquerque (1319-1323, 1329) and his aide 1o Ten. Rego Barros (1324-1326, 1328, 1330-1332). Longest: 18 Mar, three sheets; 20 May, about 40 cipher words mixed with clear.
seen.cipher: Letter cipher in telegraph words; found during vetting to be a Vigenère (standard alphabet) with an 8-letter key restarted at every word, so cipher words keep the plaintext word lengths. The telegram of 14 Mar (pagfis 1319) carries a contemporary pencil decipherment of its whole cipher text ('Pessoa que me parece bem informada diz saber por parente Rabelo que palacio está cuidadosamente minado'); pagfis 1326 has a pencil attempt 'complot ambici...' on its two words. The other telegrams have no decipherment on or with them.

prior_art.decode: Searched the DECODE dumps in research/catalogue_harvest/decode/ for Brazil, Brasil, Ceará, Setembrino and Paraguay: no record; not on DECODE.
prior_art.tomokiyo: No cryptiana page on Brazilian 20th-century or army ciphers was found by web search (site:cryptiana.web.fc2.com Brazil), and nothing in the repo's Tomokiyo-derived ledgers (known.py).
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry paper or GL.htm entry on Brazilian telegrams is known to the repo (known.py on Setembrino, Vespasiano, Pamplona, Rego Barros hits only the lead itself) and none was found by web search.
prior_art.edition: No printed edition of these telegrams was found: Portuguese web searches on 'telegramas cifrados Setembrino de Carvalho 1914', the Juazeiro sedition and the War Ministry cipher returned only general accounts of the sedition. Setembrino's memoirs and the printed Juazeiro document collections were not seen directly, so a printed clear text of some telegrams cannot be excluded; the pencil decipherment of 14 Mar is the only reading seen.
prior_art.literature: Web searches in Portuguese and English (criptografia exército 1914, telegrama cifrado Ministério da Guerra, Vigenère) found nothing on this traffic; the nearest work is the SciELO article on the Canudos (1896-97) cipher telegrams of the Arquivo Histórico do Exército, a different file.

vetting.key_check: The 1471 crib (CFIIOIZUPDYBSUDX SBHBCUDJ AFTGC = restabelecimento harmonia Pedro, all three glossed in pencil) is a Vigenère with key LBQPOHVJ restarted per word; that October key does NOT read 1470. But the decipherment pencilled on the 14 Mar telegram (pagfis 1319) gives the key MFTDBSJV in minutes, and it reads the telegrams of 14, 18, 19, 24, 29 Mar and 17 Apr directly, e.g. 18 Mar: 'dr marques porto declarou me seguinte foi feito movimento de terras nos baixos do edificio palacio governo ...'; 17 Apr: 'parece conveniente responder juiz Pernambuco dizendo que apesar nao julgar identicos casos citados contudo acatando sua decisao aguarda solucao definitiva supremo tribunal'. The 10 Mar telegram fits LETCARIV with garbles ('... chefe ... deu parte doente ... confiança'), and the 20 May telegram broke ciphertext-only to a 10-letter key in a short hill climb ('amigo sincero parente dever lealdade avisar general ...'; key not yet settled). Since a key on the file reads most of it in minutes, this is a key lookup, not an open cipher.
vetting.duplicates: known.py run on 'Setembrino', 'FSC pce 1914', 'FSC cont 1914', 'Pamplona', 'Vespasiano', 'Juazeiro', 'Rego Barros': the only hits are this lead and 1471 themselves (research/leads.json, research/latam_brazil candidates and README); no catalogue entry, target or DECODE id covers these telegrams.
vetting.closed: Pencil decipherment of the 14 Mar 1914 telegram on the file gives the per-word Vigenère key MFTDBSJV, which reads six more telegrams; see research/latam_vetting/1470_sample.txt
